title: Feed lines and connectors
blurb: The big idea before the cards.

lines.caption: A feed line carries your signal between the radio and the antenna. The most common kind is coaxial cable.
lines.label: radio to antenna

lines.caption: Coax is popular because it is easy to use. Most of it has an impedance of 50 ohms.
lines.label: 50 ohms

lines.caption: Some signal is always lost as heat on the way. The loss grows as the frequency goes up.
lines.label: higher frequency, more loss

lines.caption: Connectors join the cable to the radio and the antenna. Outdoors, tape them so that water cannot get in.
lines.label: keep water out

lines.caption: SWR tells you how well the antenna is matched to the feed line. With a good match, your power goes into the antenna.
lines.label: SWR measures the match
